additional_independently_fetched_primary.observed_fact: clear_specials_bits removes 07000 before get_unix_mode returns Unix attributes.

read_only_patch_checks.method: Independent pure-Python unified-hunk application in memory; exact old-context and old/new line-count checks. No git apply mutation.

test_semantic_review.basis: The helper first writes ordinary ZIP entries, then patches external attributes at central-header offset38. It verifies the PK0102 signature, Unix host byte at offset5, and exact stored attributes including archived mode0107755. It does not rely on unix_permissions to preserve special bits.

Offsets come from central_header_start after checking entry names and count. The archive is generated from three short fixed test inputs; checked slicing/try_from will fail setup on an unexpected layout. The two public lookup APIs exist in both2.4.2 and9.1.2.

test_semantic_review.check: Low-bit readback is deliberately version neutral
test_semantic_review.basis: Readback compares unix_mode &0777 with expected ordinary permissions. Separate raw-byte checks establish high-bit input. This accommodates2.4.2 raw mode and9.1.2 upstream-sanitized mode without pretending both return07755.

The test writes a control file, applies the exact old raw mode via real set_permissions and requires at least one07000 bit to survive. It does not skip or weaken the check when unsupported. A failure here is fixture/environment failure, not proof of old extractor vulnerability.

The test invokes extract_zipball_to_dir itself. The old production path copies payload then applies raw permissions; the candidate retains that path with mode&0777. The test compares all three exact payloads and final permissions&07777, including ordinary0644 and executable0755.

On9.1.2, removing only the local mask can still pass because upstream unix_mode already clears07000. The test proves the combined extraction invariant, not exclusive causality of the local mask. The retained original-dependency regression patch is the planned counterfactual.

The dedicated module is cfg(all(test,unix)), matching the permission behavior under test. Production nonUnix no-op remains unchanged apart from the ZipFile generic signature; no existing Windows tests are suppressed.

api_compatibility_review.zip_read: ZipFile now has R:Read+?Sized; both cfg branches use the same bound. name returns ZipResult<Cow<str>>, and candidate propagates its error. by_index/enclosed_name/is_dir plus the test writer APIs remain available. No definite type/borrow issue found by reading; not compiled.
api_compatibility_review.test_rust_semantics: The files array is Copy (string references andu32), so repeated by-value loops are valid. Closures return only offsets and release each ZipFile borrow. The new tests use a narrow parent import and explicit pretty_assertions::assert_eq, avoiding the earlier glob/prelude macro ambiguity.
api_compatibility_review.zstd_calls: Observed workspace calls use stream encode_all/decode_all, read::Decoder::new, write::Encoder::new and finish. Official0.14.3 retains these entry points, ownership shapes and io::Result interfaces. This is a source inspection, not a successful build.

dependency_review.upstream_chain: zip9.1.2 permits zstd^0.14.2; direct workspace floor0.14.3; zstd0.14.3 ->safe^8.2.0 ->sys^2.1.2. No lock resolution has verified complete old-version elimination.
dependency_review.feature_boundary: Existing default-feature choice is retained; zip9 defaults include native and compression dependencies. Version upgrades do not imply an unchanged transitive graph.
dependency_review.msrv: zip9.1.2 declares1.88; zstd0.14.3 declares1.64. Actual configured-toolchain build still required.
